name: Vigan
tagline: The best-preserved Spanish colonial town in Asia, a cobbled street of ancestral houses, horse-drawn calesas and empanada stalls.
highlight: Riding a calesa along the cobbled Calle Crisologo lit by old-fashioned lamps at dusk.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed Spanish colonial town with Calle Crisologo, ancestral houses, calesa rides, the cathedral, pottery, and Ilocano food including empanada and longganisa.

image.alt: The cobbled Calle Crisologo in Vigan lined with colonial houses

intro: Vigan, on the north-west coast of Luzon, is the best-preserved example of a planned Spanish colonial town in Asia. It was established in the 16th century as a trading post, where Chinese, Filipino and Spanish cultures met, and its surviving grid of streets and mansions combines Philippine, Chinese and European building traditions. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and in 2015 it was named one of the New 7 Wonders Cities.

The heart of the historic district is Calle Crisologo, a cobbled street lined with ancestral houses whose ground floors are stone or brick and whose upper floors are wooden with sliding capiz-shell windows. Horse-drawn calesas clatter along the street, and lamps light it in the evening. Traffic is closed at times. The nearby Plaza Salcedo, Vigan Cathedral and Plaza Burgos are the social heart.

Vigan is also a craft and food town. The Pagburnayan workshops produce large burnay clay jars, and the Ilocos region is famous for its empanadas, longganisa sausage and bagnet, crispy pork belly. A day trip can take in nearby Paoay Church and the sand dunes of Laoag. Two days is a good stay.

whyVisit.intro: Vigan is the best place in the Philippines to feel colonial history.
